Murphy was born in [[Morristown, New Jersey|Morristown]], New Jersey but grew up in [[Sparta Township, New Jersey|Sparta Township]].Brown, Clifton. [https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9C0DEFD81430F936A25751C0A9679C8B63 "COLLEGE BASKETBALL; The Irish Pound Rutgers To Win Eighth in a Row"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', February 15, 2001; accessed October 4, 2008. "It was a happy homecoming for Notre Dame's star junior forward, Troy Murphy (18 points, 5 rebounds), a native of Sparta, N.J." He attended the [[Delbarton School]] and the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|University of Notre Dame]], both of which are Roman Catholic schools. During his time at Notre Dame, he was a two-time consensus [[All-America]]n before declaring himself for the [[2001 NBA draft]], where he was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 14th overall pick.Stephenson, Colin. [http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2010/11/delbarton_product_troy_murphy.html "Delbarton product Troy Murphy starts in Nets debut"], ''[[The Star-Ledger]]'', November 4, 2010; accessed February 15, 2011. Murphy has since graduated from [[Columbia University]].{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bn6tgI8J0vY#t=120 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/bn6tgI8J0vY |archive-date=2021-12-13 |url-status=live|title=Troy Murphy, former NBA player, talks transition into Columbia life|last=Columbia Daily Spectator|date=April 27, 2014|via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} ==High school== Murphy was a standout performer for [[Delbarton School]] in [[Morristown, New Jersey|Morristown]], New Jersey and coach Dan Whalen.{{cite journal |last=Noie |first=Tom |title=Notre Dame's Dynamic Duo – Troy Murphy and Ruth Riley expected to boost both the men's and women's basketball teams at Notre Dame |date=January 2001 |journal=Basketball Digest |volume=28 |issue=3 |access-date=May 29, 2007 |url=http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0FCJ/is_3_28/ai_68362620 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060624123416/http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0FCJ/is_3_28/ai_68362620 |archive-date=June 24, 2006 |via=[[FindArticles]] |url-status=usurped}} His breakout year was as a sophomore when he averaged 20.5 points per game and 11.8 rebounds, earning first team all-county honors. He followed up his sophomore year with a successful junior campaign, averaging 23.5 points and 10.5 rebounds and All-State honors. His senior year would be his most successful season as he led Delbarton to a 20–6 record and the state quarterfinals. For the season he averaged 33.0 points per game (on 56.8 percent shooting), to lead the state in scoring along with 14.8 rebounds and 3.2 blocks per game. At the end of the season he was named Morris County Player of the Year by the ''[[Star-Ledger|Newark Star-Ledger]]'' and the most valuable player for his team at the prestigious [[Capital Classic (all-star game)|Capital Classic]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] ==College career== Murphy played college basketball at the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|University of Notre Dame]]. He led the Irish in scoring and rebounding in each of his three seasons, averaging 21.8 points and 9.2 rebounds during the 2000–01 campaign. A consensus first-team All-American as a junior and sophomore, he is one of 10 Irish players to earn consensus All-American honors (which includes six players named on more than one occasion). Murphy shared [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Conference Player of the Year]] honors with [[Troy Bell]] of [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]] in 2001 and joined an elite group of four players—[[Chris Mullin (basketball)|Chris Mullin]] ([[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]), [[Patrick Ewing]] ([[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]) and [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]] ([[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]])—as the only two-time winners of the award. He was named to the John R. Wooden Award All-America Team for the second consecutive year, finished fifth in the balloting for the Wooden Award and was among the top three finalists for the Naismith player-of-the-year honor. A first-team all-Big East selection for two seasons, Murphy also was named the Big East Rookie of the Year in 1999. He became just the fifth player in Notre Dame history to score more than 2,000 career points and finished his career fifth on the all-time scoring list with 2,011 points. Murphy is the only player to score more than 2,000 points and grab more than 900 rebounds (924) in 94 career games. He left Notre Dame with career averages of 21.4 points and 9.8 rebounds. Murphy was a starter in 93 games during his career and scored in double figures in 92 of those 94 contests. In addition to finishing fifth on the all-time career scoring list, upon his departure from the university, he ranked second in blocked shots (126), free throws made (587) and free throws attempted (755), sixth in rebounding and field goals made (680) and ninth in field goals attempted (1,370).{{cite web|url=http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/042001aaa.html|title=Murphy Declares For The Draft|access-date=December 13, 2007|archive-date=October 12, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081012044138/http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/042001aaa.html|url-status=dead}} On January 23, 2016, Murphy was inducted into Notre Dame's Ring of Honor. ==Professional career== === Golden State Warriors (2001–2007) === Murphy was selected 14th overall in the [[2001 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. After starting slowly, he showed promise toward the end of the season. He realized this promise in his second pro season, averaging a double-double – 11.7 pts and 10.2 boards – and finishing second in [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] voting. He also started the [[Rookie Challenge]] as the Sophomores' power forward. However, his three-point shooting that was a huge part of his college success was nearly absent, as he only attempted 14 three-pointers during the year, making five. He spent the next offseason working extensively on his outside shooting; however, he never got much of a chance to test out his new jumper in [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04]] after a series of injuries limited him to 28 games, with no starts. However, he did attempt 17 threes in those games. With that part of his arsenal seemingly ready to go, Murphy spent the following offseason working on strength and conditioning as he looked to be a more well-rounded and complete player. While he had one injury scare the next season, he played in 70 games, and rediscovered his three-point shot, attempting nearly three per game. He averaged 15.4 points and 10.8 rebounds and finished 22nd in Western Conference All-Star voting that year. His numbers dropped off slightly in [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06]] to 14.0 and 10.0 per game. === Indiana Pacers (2007–2010) === On January 17, 2007, Murphy was involved in an 8-player trade that sent him, [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]], [[Ike Diogu]], and [[Keith McLeod]] to the [[Indiana Pacers]] for [[Stephen Jackson]], [[Al Harrington]], [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], and [[Josh Powell]].{{cite news|url=http://www.mopsquad.com/artman2/publish/Indiana_Pacers_72/Pacers_Warriors_announce_8-player_deal.htm|title=Pacers, Warriors announce 8-player deal|agency=Associated Press|date=January 17, 2007|access-date=December 23, 2007}} During his time with the Pacers, Murphy's three-point shot improved even more. Against the [[Utah Jazz]] on March 10, 2009, Murphy made seven out of his first eight three-pointers in the first half. === New Jersey Nets (2010–2011) === On August 11, 2010, the Pacers traded Murphy to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in a four-team, five-player deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt1|title=Pacers get Collison from Hornets in 4-team trade|date=August 11, 2010|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 11, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530080120/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt1|archive-date=May 30, 2011}} ===Boston Celtics (2011)=== On February 23, 2011, the Warriors reacquired Murphy and a second-round pick in exchange for [[Brandan Wright]] and [[Dan Gadzuric]].{{cite web| title = Warriors Acquire Troy Murphy And 2012 Second Round Draft Pick From New Jersey|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_murphy_pick_022311.html|date=February 23, 2011|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On February 27, Murphy and the Warriors reached a buyout agreement. He was [[Waivers (NBA)|waived]] in time to be playoff-eligible for a new team.{{cite news|last=Kawakami|first=Tim|title=Breaking news: Warriors buy out Troy Murphy (and why it's a wise move)|date=February 27, 2011|newspaper=[[San Jose Mercury News]]|url=http://blogs.mercurynews.com/kawakami/2011/02/27/breaking-news-warriors-buy-out-troy-murphy-and-why-its-a-wise-move|access-date=February 28, 2011|quote=Murphy had to be waived before Tuesday to remain eligible for a playoff roster on a new team. CLARIFICATION: There is a later deadline for signing with a new team.}}{{cite news|title=Warriors, Murphy reach buyout agreement|date=February 28, 2011|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/02/28/warriors.murphy.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2|access-date=February 28, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303083903/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/02/28/warriors.murphy.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2|archive-date=March 3, 2011}}[[File:Troy Murphy Celtics.jpg|thumb|right|Murphy with the Celtics]] On March 2, 2011, Murphy signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] for the remainder of the [[2010-11 NBA season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/030211-celtics-sign-murphy.html|title=Celtics Sign Troy Murphy|work=Nba.com|access-date=August 3, 2012}} On April 22, 2011, Murphy played in his first career playoff game, a first-round game against the [[New York Knicks]]. === Los Angeles Lakers (2011–2012) === On December 17, 2011, Murphy signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2011-12 NBA season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/111218lakersign_troymurphy.html|title=Lakers Sign Troy Murphy|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2011|access-date=August 3, 2012}} Over the season, he averaged 3.2 points in 16.2 minutes per game. ===Dallas Mavericks (2012)=== On November 2, 2012, Murphy signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2012–13 NBA season]], replacing [[Eddy Curry]].{{cite web|author=Tim MacMahon|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4692407/mavs-make-troy-murphy-eddy-curry-moves-official|title=Mavs make Troy Murphy, Eddy Curry moves official|date=November 2, 2012 |publisher=Espn.go.com|access-date=November 2, 2012}} Murphy's final game in the NBA was played on November 28, 2012, in a 78 - 101 loss to the Chicago Bulls where he recorded 7 points, 2 rebounds and 2 blocks. He was waived the very next day on November 29 when Dallas signed [[guard (basketball)|guard]] [[Derek Fisher]].{{cite news|title=Mavericks sign free-agent guard Derek Fisher; Waive Troy
